meta.source: US DRI 2019-2020 (IOM/NASEM), NIH ODS Fact Sheets, Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025

citations.primary: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Energy, Carbohydrate, Fiber, Fat, Fatty Acids, Cholesterol, Protein, and Amino Acids. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press, 2005.
citations.vitamins: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Thiamin, Riboflavin, Niacin, Vitamin B6, Folate, Vitamin B12, Pantothenic Acid, Biotin, and Choline. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press, 1998.
citations.minerals: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium, Phosphorus, Magnesium, Vitamin D, and Fluoride. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press, 1997.
citations.trace_elements: Institute of Medicine. Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium, and Zinc. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press, 2001.
citations.dietary_guidelines: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and U.S. Department of Agriculture. 2020–2025 Dietary Guidelines for Americans. 9th Edition. December 2020.

notes: Values rounded to whole units as per policy
UL values enforced as safety limits where established
Energy-scaled nutrients (fiber, added sugars) calculated dynamically
Sex-neutral 'other' uses averaged values where male/female differ
Macros (calories, protein, fat, carbs) calculated by macro engine
